title: Custom code and snippets
when_to_use: Adding analytics, pixels, chat widgets, CSS/JS, or anything the user phrases as put in header/footer/functions.php.
principles: Outcome over file path: “put in header” usually means print in <head> (wp_head), not edit header.php.
Never edit the active theme’s header.php / footer.php / functions.php — theme updates wipe it; block themes often have no usable header.php; edits are hard to undo.
Prefer an Ahentic code-snippet ability when available; if that ability is missing, say so (missing_ability) and give a safe manual workaround — do not invent file edits.
Before adding analytics/tracking, list plugins — warn if Site Kit, MonsterInsights, ExactMetrics, GA Google Analytics, or similar already injects tags.
Do not default to installing Site Kit when the user pasted a measurement ID or script and wants that snippet on the site.
Free-tier custom code is HTML/CSS/JS; freeform PHP hooks are Premium / missing until available — do not fake PHP via CSS.
steps: Clarify whether they want a literal snippet/ID or a full analytics plugin setup with Google account flow.
Call ahentic/list-plugins to detect existing analytics/tag managers.
If a snippet ability exists: upsert with location head/body_open/footer, HITL preview of exact code, avoid duplicate tags.

If no snippet ability yet: set missing_ability (e.g. ahentic/upsert-code-snippet), explain not to edit theme files, and offer: paste via a trusted snippets plugin they already have, or Customizer Additional CSS for CSS-only, or wait for Ahentic snippets.
For PHP/login-rename/server redirects: explain PHP is not free-form on free; offer Premium path or capability request — do not write PHP into the Ahentic plugin.
anti_patterns: Installing Site Kit every time someone says “add GA”.
Stacking a second analytics injector when one is already active.
Dumping arbitrary PHP into Ahentic’s plugin files.
